meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

They can rent the entire hotel.

examples.trans: Stop, bring me a drink, huh?
I brought the ice cream.
What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Так клянусь, мне повар знакомый рассказывал.
examples.trans: I swear, a cook I know told me.

examples.text: Шейх Настю? Я тебя умоляю, кому она нужна?
examples.trans: The sheikh, Nastya? I beg you, who needs her?

examples.text: В смысле, Настя, ты мне нужна!
examples.trans: I mean, Nastya, I need you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Today is your day off.
Wait, are you Russian?
Stop, bring me a drink, huh?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: Do you want to taste some more?
Try the tea with bread rings.
I'll try one more time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, taste it yourself.

examples.text: Ой, спасибо тебе, я уже год так не расслаблялась.
examples.trans: Oh, thank you, I have not relaxed like this in a year.
Thank you, no need.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.trans: Let us make it one more time.

examples.text: Давай я отнесу, это молекулярное блюдо, надо в номере доделать.
examples.trans: Let me take it, this is a molecular dish, it must be finished in the room.
Come on, infidels, let us hurry along.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'верный'). Common masculine noun meaning 'infidels / unbelievers' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Come on, infidels, let us hurry along.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть неверный.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always infidels.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'торапливаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'hurry along'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и поторапливаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and hurry along on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют поторапливаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to hurry along.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'bring / haul', paired with 'потащить'.

examples.trans: Lyova, bring the cheese and the pear.
Bring it over here faster!
Bring the clothespin quickly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Get lost!
Bring it over here faster!
Louis, come here quickly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'faster', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Bring the pear faster, Lyova!
Try to make it fast and strong.
Bring it over here faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костян, ты не боишься, что Настя отнесёт шейху заказ?
examples.trans: Kostyan, are you not afraid that Nastya will take the order to the sheikh?
Well, is it ready? I will serve it myself.
Wait, are you Russian?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, how did it go?

examples.text: Шеф, там Катю увели в этой штуке!
examples.trans: Chef, they led Katya away in that outfit!

examples.text: Если Катя в гареме, может, и Настя там?
examples.trans: If Katya is in the harem, maybe Nastya is there too?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'saw / did you see'.

examples.text: А меня шейх на свидание позвал.
examples.trans: And the sheikh invited me on a date.
Did you see, she made a gesture!

examples.text: Скажу, что ты нанял людей меня пытать. И не видать вам квартиры!
examples.trans: I'll say that you hired people to torture me. And you'll never see that flat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь она живёт в его гареме.
examples.trans: Now she lives in his harem.

examples.text: Шейх Настю? Я тебя умоляю, кому она нужна?
examples.trans: The sheikh, Nastya? I beg you, who needs her?
Did you see, she made a gesture!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'gesture' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Did you see, she made a gesture!
He wants to fulfill his marital duty!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Did you see, she made a gesture!
Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'like, sort of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Like they gave her the ring!

examples.text: А она типа не при делах.
examples.trans: And she acts like she had nothing to do with it.

examples.text: Да я не про это. Кто этот тип в коридоре?
examples.trans: That's not what I mean. Who was that guy in the corridor?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'signet / gem ring' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он продал этот перстень и уехал за границу.
examples.trans: He sold that ring and moved abroad.
Can you imagine how much such a ring costs?
I wish I had a ring like that!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ask for', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.en: to repeat, to say or do again
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вторить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to repeat', paired with 'повторять'.

examples.trans: They are asking to repeat the ice cream for the room.
This will never happen again!
Right, let's go over it again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The hotel is geared toward well-off people.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.
A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Только обеспеченный человек снимет у нас номер.
examples.trans: Only a wealthy person will book a room with us.

examples.text: Через час у шейха ужин, а это заказ в номер.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'again', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They are taking cognac ice cream again!

Rain again.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are carrying', paired with 'понести'.

examples.text: Одна девушка отнесла ему заказ и пропала.
examples.trans: One girl brought him an order and vanished.

examples.text: Костян, ты не боишься, что Настя отнесёт шейху заказ?
examples.trans: Kostyan, are you not afraid that Nastya will take the order to the sheikh?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Excuse me, this is our electrician.

examples.text: Мне подружки из этого отеля рассказывали.
examples.trans: My girlfriends from that hotel told me.

examples.text: Извините, я ничего не видел, пойду всё переделаю.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I saw nothing, I will go redo everything.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cognac' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пап, а ты думаешь, как коньяк на стадион пронести?
examples.trans: Dad, are you thinking about how to sneak cognac into the stadium?

examples.text: Температура замерзания коньяка — минус тридцать градусов.
examples.trans: The freezing temperature of cognac is minus thirty degrees.

examples.text: Через пару минут мороженое из коньяка готово.
examples.trans: In a couple of minutes the cognac ice cream is ready.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: A truly prosperous guest will treat himself to a suite.
They definitely want to take all the rings.
Lyolya will definitely come!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: And he would like to get to know you more closely.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They can rent the entire hotel.
A lively shift is beginning.

examples.text: Ваш муж хочет навестить вас после ужина.
examples.trans: Your husband wants to visit you after dinner.

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away', paired with 'забирать'.

examples.trans: They definitely want to take all the rings.
He will withdraw the statement.
I'll take the keys.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: We will cook it better than anyone right now!

examples.text: Слушай, сейчас шеф получит наш перстень.
examples.trans: Listen, now the Chef will get our ring.

examples.text: Всё понятно, сейчас шейха напоят, а он их отблагодарит.
examples.trans: Everything is clear, now they will get the sheikh drunk and he will reward them.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will do', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Шеф, мы с Федей сами сделаем!
examples.trans: Chef, Fedya and I will make it ourselves!
Let us make it one more time.
I will make everything myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let us make it one more time.
Do you want to taste some more?
Anything else?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Stop wasting ingredients!
Please, walk carefully.
Make one more chocolate fondant.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'portion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will make one more portion right now.
The waiter brought two portions of salad.

examples.text: И ещё две порции трески с миндалём!
examples.trans: And two more portions of cod with almonds!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: But there are very wealthy guests.
Do you want to taste some more?
In a chef's hat it will look very suspicious.

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'pleased, was liked', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.
Did you like the film?
Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'guest (female)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: But there are very wealthy guests.

examples.text: А вот это тот самый состоятельный гость.
examples.trans: And this is that very wealthy guest.
